correctness.rationale: For the six-vertex complete tripartite octahedron K_{2,2,2}, enumerated all 12 graph edges and all 8 perfect matchings as disjoint triples; obtained exactly (12,24,8) nonempty faces of P and (12,30,8) of the ordinary matching complex M. Every graph edge is contained in two perfect matchings, intersections of distinct perfect-matching facets yield exactly 12 nerve edges and no higher nerve faces, with the cube degree/distance signature (12,12,4) and an explicitly checked 8-vertex cube isomorphism. The facet-intersection construction is natural for all graph automorphisms; the nonempty-face-poset incidence maps are equivariant, order-reversing, and have extensive compositions, so order-complex/nerve homotopy is equivariant rather than only a Betti-number equality. The complement consists of precisely six nonextendible 2-edge matchings, all added 1-simplices with their endpoints already in connected P; C_*(M,P) is concentrated in degree 1 and the integral long exact sequence gives 0->H1(P;Z)->H1(M;Z)->Z[B]_or->0. This is a primitive sublattice (free quotient rank six), with ranks 5 and 11. An independent combinatorial implementation checked all 48 full signed-coordinate automorphisms, the exact ten conjugacy-class rational cycle-character values, decomposition by sign-twisted standard S4 and the 3-pair permutation character, center trace +1 and its -6 signed relative trace. A cube edge-reversing stabilizer at every edge forces H1(P;Z)^G=0. No integral splitting or higher-graph theorem is inferred. The proof uses exact finite graph enumeration plus general poset and relative-chain arguments, not the source VERIFY_OK line.
residual_risks: Integral G-module is the concrete cube cycle lattice and six-edge extension; no indecomposable decomposition or integral equivariant splitting is proved.
The nerve equivalence is of geometric realizations, not an isomorphism between the two different-dimensional simplicial complexes.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge distinct complete equivariant perfect-matching nerve and integral relative inclusion for CP(3)=K_{2,2,2). The previously published exact same-graph SCOPE result is for the ordinary matching complex, whose rank-11 and rational character do not alone identify the perfect-only facet nerve, its natural integer cycle submodule or the signed quotient. Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega use nerve methods but classify honeycomb graphs; Chandrakar–Singh count bad matchings and classify polygonal line tilings and ladders, not CP(3). The generic equivariant nerve lemma is prior mathematical infrastructure, not the explicit cube nerve and integral extension. Related Resultary cube, cuboctahedral and 2-matching results concern different graph complexes. A broad search is not a priority certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite computation may already give the same cube nerve and signed relative module; global historical priority is not certified.
Prior ordinary-complex representation constrains the rational answer once the embedding is known, so the genuinely independent content is the natural integral equivariant nerve/inclusion.
Generic equivariant nerve theorem is known and should not be claimed as a new mathematical principle.

value.rationale: The octahedral graph is the smallest nontrivial cocktail-party graph and a Platonic dual of the cube. The perfect-extendibility matching subcomplex is a canonical object in studied topological matching theory, and its full equivariant cube cycle lattice is a natural exact structural invariant. The six nonextendible two-edge matchings precisely describe how topology and symmetry change when moving from perfect-only to ordinary matchings; the primitive integral relative sequence is more than reprinting a Betti count or the old rational character. The small finite result is self-contained, correctly scoped, and plausibly reusable as a minimal symmetry-aware example in perfect matching/relative homology work. No arbitrary slice or downstream grand theorem is claimed.
residual_risks: The statement is restricted to the octahedron; no full higher cross-polytope family theorem follows.
The extension is exact but equivariant integral splitting and indecomposable lattice classification remain unproved.

limitations: Best-of-knowledge originality, not proof against all unindexed historical literature.
No generalization to other cocktail-party graphs; no integral equivariant splitting.
